items.stem: The SI unit of work is:
Which of the following is a case where work is done (scientifically)?
items.markingKey: (c) A boy climbing stairs is a case where work is done (scientifically). The others: a porter standing still with a load on his head – a case where no work is done (scientifically); a satellite moving in a circular orbit due to gravity – a case where no work is done (scientifically); pushing a wall that does not move – a case where no work is done (scientifically).
options: pushing a wall that does not move
a porter standing still with a load on his head
a satellite moving in a circular orbit due to gravity

items.answer: Yes. As it falls, potential energy decreases and kinetic energy increases by the same amount; the sum stays constant (ignoring air resistance).

items.stem: A loader pushes a 1000 N drum up a smooth ramp 8 m long onto a truck 1.5 m high. Find the effort needed (ignore friction) and the mechanical advantage of the ramp.
items.markingKey: Work in = work out: E × 8 = 1000 × 1.5 ⇒ E = 188 N; MA = 1000/188 = 5.33 (= length/height).

items.stem: Can a machine give more work output than input? Explain.
items.answer: No. By conservation of energy, output can at most equal input; friction makes it less.
